INVERTS THE VOC PATTERN. There is no subscribed permanent capital: contributions were called as needed and non-payment forfeited the share. Capital is therefore immobile in the sense that it cannot be withdrawn, but it was never locked in as a fixed sum either. DECIDES THE HARRIS DISPUTE ON THE STRUCTURAL QUESTION. D'Amico adds that all major decisions including the appointment of managers involved senior staff in consultation with the head, 'who could not make unilateral decisions'. Collective governance inside a form with no legal personality.

Inapplicable: MG1=contract, so there is no membership whose entry could be restricted. Entitlement runs through the partnership agreement and the prospective-fund investment. Recruitment data exist — 43 per cent of hires between 1836 and 1862 came from outside the Nakai's home province of Ōmi, against houses where over 90 per cent shared a common origin — but employment is not entry to the entity, and coding it here would answer a different question.

THE CELL THAT MAKES THIS A COUNTER-CASE. No charter, no grant, no authorising act. The samurai authorities enforced private contracts and distinguished kane kuji from hon kuji, but 'flatly refused to handle cases related to the settlement of accounts in partnerships, explicitly designating them as one of the primary categories of non-adjudicable issues (nakama-goto)'. The law offered no tool for forming a business. These entities arose against a standing refusal, not merely in its absence.
Trading and brewing enterprises across some forty stores. No pious or mutual-provision limb.
No monopoly franchise attaches to the entity. Contrast kabu_nakama and the alleenrecht, where the privilege is the asset.

THE DEFINITIONAL CELL. The fictive household is an identity wrapper in the strict sense: a name that looks like a person, holds assets, signs documents and is registered, with no body behind it. Yamahiroya-Chōbe of 1870 is the limiting case — 'a store name recognized as a member of the neighborhood (chō) without a flesh-and-blood head in existence'.

Registered and legible to the state precisely as a household. A store clerk placed the five-year-old Iwanosuke's seal on the teraokuri shōmon in 1806; clerks cited his youth on the 1827 shūmon aratame-chō and, after he died in 1807, switched the excuse to sickness in 1829 and 1835. The register recorded a household that did not exist. Legibility achieved without the state ever conferring entity status.

Outside partners at Sendai were explicitly passive — 'the four together served as passive partners' — while non-kin professional managers ran the stores. But managers could hold shares, so the capital-labour line is not clean.

Applicable because CF1 is P. The Sōma manager's share appears in the loss base ('losses will be divided by 19 shares'), so the agent bears some capital loss — but see LR6, where the same clause is ambiguous. Low, and dependent on the same verification.

Multiple principals throughout: Nishikawa Denji formed 1741-57 by twenty-one investors holding forty shares; Sōma 1783 founded by the main house together with Nakai Shinsaburō, itself a fictive household. Fictive households could become founding partners in further fictive households — entities compounding, not merely persons.

The defining arrangement: an investor entrusts capital to an agent who trades and lends it, then repays principal and a share of profits. Peng Daya, verbatim: 從韃主至僞太子僞公主皆付回回以銀 — from the Mongol emperor down to the princes and princesses, all entrust their silver to the Hui-hui. Coded 1 rather than P despite the Fakhr al-Din case where the ortoq added his own capital; see the note on CF3.

THE CELL THIS FORM EXISTS TO CARRY, and the attested instance is firmer than the generalisation. Direct: Ogedei kept investing in an ortoq through repeated failures, and Enkhbold writes of that case flatly — 'In this example, Ogedei bore all liability for any losses, while his ortoq bore no liability for the loss of capital' (Juvayni 1958, 209-210). Corroborated by Rashid al-Din 725, where investors could do nothing when partners lost capital and 'tried hard to compensate their ortoqs'. Downgraded from high to medium because the step from that instance to the form is inside the paragraph governed by 'it can be hypothesized'. DISAGREEMENT RECORDED, NOT RESOLVED: Lin 2013, 229 holds that it is unclear whether the ortoq were granted any form of entity or owner-shielding, for lack of sources; Enkhbold contends against him. Enkhbold's own framing is 'Evidence of the liability borne by the Mongols or their partners is extremely fragmentary', and the generalisation is introduced as 'Thus, it can be hypothesized that'. The Fakhr al-Din leg of it rests on Vassaf's SILENCE about the Tibi family's obligations. Confidence downgraded accordingly; .NR is a defensible alternative if the maintainer judges the hypothesis too thin.

One investor, one travelling partner is the attested core. Two complications held at medium: an ortoq could hold several partnerships simultaneously (the Berke/Hulegu evidence), which is several bilateral contracts rather than one multilateral one; and Enkhbold reads the Fakhr al-Din case as possibly 'one travelling partner and several investors', but the modal is his, not the source's — 'it is also possible that'. The coding does not exceed the hedge.

Profits divided at a predetermined ratio after deducting travel expenses; the agent's return moves with the venture's outcome.

Proportional shares, not a fixed claim, and the ratios are recorded: a mere one-tenth to the principal in the early years of Qubilai's reign (Otagi 1973, 15), and 70/30 to the Yuan government against the merchants in 1284 (Allsen 1989, 118). Articulation .NR — the ratios are reported from Yuan Shi and Otagi, not quoted as contract language.

Observed absence. A bilateral capital-labour contract mutualises nothing across a membership; the ortoq's risk is transferred between two parties, not pooled among many. Same reading as commenda, qirad and isqa.
Inapplicable where LR4 is 0. Propagated .NA per CONTRIBUTING §4.

THE SOURCE SAYS IT IS UNKNOWN, IN TERMS: 'The maximum time of validity of a Mongol-ortoq partnership is not entirely clear.' Both readings are attested and neither is dominant — Nicolo and Maffeo Polo were free to leave the Golden Horde once they had sold the wares entrusted by Berke, and maritime merchants were contracted for a single voyage, but 'some trusted and experienced ortoqs might have been continuously employed by their Mongol investors, since the duration of these partnerships was at the will of the partners.' Do NOT import single-venture from commenda; that is the inference this row exists to refuse.

Capital is entrusted per venture and per investor rather than held as a common fund; an ortoq holding several partnerships at once held them separately. Medium — Enkhbold nowhere describes the accounting, and this is read off the contracting pattern.

The claim arises from the entrustment, not from membership in a body. The term ortoq designates a merchant standing in a personal gift-exchange relationship with a high-status Mongol or funded by the Mongol government.

ENDICOTT-WEST 1989 IS THE SOURCE THAT WOULD FILL THIS AND SHE IS NOT IN HAND. Enkhbold shows ortoqs carrying paiza and jarliq and drawing on the jam relay system, which is a grant of privilege by the ruler, but says nothing about what authorised the partnership itself. Private contract, customary practice and state charter are all live and the source does not choose.
Trade and money-lending for gain throughout; no charitable or mutual-provision purpose anywhere in the record.

The paiza is the wrapper: an ortoq carrying one could exact provisions and mounts from the relay stations, and Enkhbold notes that restricting edicts 'were frequently ignored, and many merchants wilfully evaded taxation and freely used relay stations'. CAUTION: FP3's definition reads 'confers legal-status or access arbitrage for its PRINCIPALS', and here the arbitrage accrues to the agent. The characteristic is written around a form whose beneficiaries are its members; a capital-labour contract has no such symmetry.

Endicott-West's cell. Official oversight and taxation are described as a LATER reform ('Some Mongol leaders made administrative and economic reforms, starting in the second half of the thirteenth century'), so registration is not evidence about the early regime. Left .NR rather than 0 — nobody asks whether the early ortoq was registered.
Unchanged from the equity regime: the Mongol side supplies capital and the ortoq supplies enterprise. What changes is the legal character of the capital.

REVERSED FROM ortoq_equity, AND THIS IS THE FINDING. 'Consequently, ortoqs were completely liable for the loans they took, which extended beyond partnership capital to their private properties' (Enkhbold 2019, 543-544). Same value as isqa, reached from the opposite starting point. TWO LIMITS ADDED AFTER READING ENDICOTT-WEST 1989. First, no commercial contract survives in the Chinese sources of the Yuan period, so this cell rests entirely on Persian narrative — Juvayni, Rashid al-Din, Vassaf — and cannot be corroborated from the Yuan side. Second, her Yuan debt material runs the OTHER WAY and must not be read into it: the 1318 decree on absconding debtors, the 1300 remission of interest for soldiers at Qara Qorum, and Wang Yun's debtors selling their possessions and their wives and children all concern the ortoq's BORROWERS, not his liability to his principal. CONFIDENCE HELD AT MEDIUM, NOT HIGH. Two limits apply to the loan regime as much as to the equity one. Endicott-West 1989, 132 states that no commercial contract has survived in the Chinese sources of the Yuan period, so nothing on the Yuan side can corroborate or refute the Persian narrative this rests on. And part of Enkhbold's claim is inference from the instrument rather than attestation — 'A loan, by contrast, makes a borrower's liability unlimited' is a definitional step, not a datum. No liability cell in either ortoq regime now stands above medium.

Borrower and lender, with a guarantor standing outside the contract rather than as a third principal. TENSION RECORDED: Endicott-West 1989, 132 describes the arrangement as one in which investors 'pool their capital and entrust it to a manager', and the 泉府司 disbursed the funds of emperor, heir apparent, empress and princes through a single office — which would read multilateral on the investor side. Held at bilateral/medium because she is glossing the commenda generally there and no Yuan instrument survives to settle it.

Liability reaches private property and beyond it to the person: 'Properties could be seized, and if they were insufficient to clear the debt, defaulters and their families were taken into slavery' (Rashid al-Din 1998, 726). Coded several rather than joint because the guarantor's obligation is a separate undertaking — 'the guarantor unconditionally guaranteed the full payment of the debt' — not co-liability among partners. Under loan financing the return to the Mongol side is a fixed claim, not a proportional share — the Yuan government lent to ortoqs at 0.8 per cent a month in the early years of Qubilai's reign (Allsen 1989, 119). Medium because Enkhbold does not say the two arrangements were mutually exclusive in practice and both are attested in the Yuan period; the value records the loan contract's own logic.
Observed absence; nothing is mutualised across a membership.
Inapplicable where LR4 is 0. Propagated .NA.

The call option is gone: the ortoq keeps the residual above the interest and bears the whole downside, to the point of enslavement. Same value as isqa. The pair ortoq_equity/ortoq_loan therefore separates on LR6 within a single institution — the first time the census records a form traversing the agent-loss-exposure axis rather than sitting at a point on it. Unknown, as for ortoq_equity. Enkhbold's statement that the maximum validity 'is not entirely clear' is not periodised, so it cannot be resolved for the later regime either.
Per-contract accounting; no common fund.
The claim arises from the loan instrument.

The Yuan definition constitutes the ortoq by state disbursement: 吏學指南 (preface 1301) glosses wo-t'o as the name whereby government funds used for trade were distributed to earn interest, and the 泉府司 handled 'affairs pertaining to the expenditure and income of government funds for the emperor as well as the heir apparent, the empress, and the princes'. MEDIUM, AND THE HEDGE IS THE SOURCE'S OWN: 'no commercial contract as such has come down to us in the Chinese sources of the Yuan period'. What is chartered is the merchant's STATUS and the disbursement apparatus; the partnership instrument is unrecoverable, so state-charter describes the authorisation of the actor rather than of the contract.

Trade and money-lending, the latter at compounded rates the sources put at 100 per cent a year — 'one ding of capital will be 1,024 ding in ten years' (Peng Daya). The Yuan attempt to mandate 3 per cent failed; Dunhuang contracts show 200-300 per cent on some private loans.

DISAGREEMENT RECORDED AS A CODING, NOT A VERDICT. The wrapper is real — paiza, jarliq, relay mounts, and arms-bearing granted by decree in 1263 to Mongols, Uighurs, Muslims, ortoy and daruyaci alike. But Enkhbold has the restricting edicts 'frequently ignored', while Endicott-West documents sustained curtailment: commercial tax from 1263 on 'people who use government silver to engage in commerce'; household taxes 當差 explicitly NOT remitted per 1271 decrees quoting Mongke, exemption available only by registering as a military household; no exemption from state service; weapons surrendered in port from 1293-09-26; a 1309 memorial rescinding Muslim merchants' imperial letters, tiger tablets and post-horse rights, granted. Privileges return after Qubilai and especially once the 泉府司 lapses in 1311. Coded 1 because the form confers the arbitrage; medium because the state kept clawing it back. NOT P — P is structural half-presence, not a value that oscillates.

斡脱戶 wo-t'o hu IS A NAMED HOUSEHOLD-REGISTRATION CATEGORY IN YUAN LAW, and the tradition names it in its own decrees — 通制條格 2 quotes imperial 聖旨 and princely 令旨 'concerning the sundry ortoy households'. Registers exist behind it: a 1252 original and a 1263 supplementary listing 2,953 Muslim civilian households at Chung-tu (Wang Yun). A dedicated bureaucracy with a datable life: Boral Qarasun placed in charge 1253-01-09; 斡脱總管府 established 1268-01-13; 斡脱所 regional offices 1272-09-05; renamed 泉府司 1280-11-30; abolished 1284, reinstated 1285 under Dasman; given jurisdiction over the Maritime Trade Bureaus 1286; regional 行泉府司 from 1288. CAVEAT ON THE END DATE: the 泉府司 was abolished in 1311 'apparently forever', after which the ortoy were 'comparatively free of restrictions and controls' — this cell describes c.1253-1311, not the whole life of the form.

NEW CELL, AND A DELIBERATE .NR. Endicott-West describes a virtual state-merchant monopoly over the most valuable maritime goods — at Ch'uan-chou gold, silver, copper, iron and slaves were barred to private merchants — and the pre-Qubilai role of ortoy in tax farming 撲買, which she states did not continue into Qubilai's era. Neither satisfies FP2 as written: it requires an exclusive right or franchise HELD AS PROPERTY, and an exclusionary trade regime run by the state in its own interest is not a franchise the ortoq owns. Coded .NR rather than P or 0 because the question in FP2's terms is not one the source asks.

Freely transferable and inheritable, evidenced by the instruments themselves: shares in the 1878 Qu-Li rice mill changed hands several times within a decade; Yuan Baozhai's four shares in the Zhengxunxiang were sold on his death to a medicinal herb shop 'that may have simply viewed the shares as an income-producing asset'; the Tongren tang founders' stake fell to half a share among twenty-one shareholders before being bought back in the 1880s. RESTRAINTS DO NOT DEFEAT THE VALUE, per the maintainer's ruling and the bazacle_mill precedent: Zigong well-drilling contracts commonly stipulate that 'a partner may not transfer his shares to someone else on his own' and the Shenxin mill required unanimous consent, but Zelin reads these as a right of first refusal and records that Zigong shares 'changed hands frequently' regardless. A procedural restraint on WHO may buy is not a limit on whether the interest is alienable.

THE CENSUS'S FIRST CI4=1, AND IT SHOULD BE READ AS SUCH. Warrant is the Mutaishangtang dispute of 1911: the shop kept a ledger of shares held and sold, and 'each shareholder was issued a share certificate on which the number of shares held was clearly written. It was on the basis of these certificates that profits were distributed' — the Ying heirs lost precisely because they had no certificate to present. The claim runs with the instrument, not the person or the lineage. Confidence medium rather than high because the counter-evidence is real: transfer restrictions made the identity of the BUYER relevant in some firms, and Zelin nowhere says a certificate could be transferred without the partnership's knowledge. Before this cell is used in any comparative claim, note that CI4 previously took no positive value anywhere in the census.
Joint capital, 合本 heben, pooled into a single fund against which shares are issued; the 1655 Mentou gou coal contract divides one pit into 45 shares across landowner, developers and new investors.

Withdrawal at will is not addressed. The 上下节 shangxia jie recapitalisations at Zigong and the 1873 Shanxi restructuring show capital being restructured — partners leaving, others increasing or decreasing their stake, new shares issued — which implies exit was possible but says nothing about whether contributed capital could be withdrawn unilaterally.

Proportional, not fixed: 'if there are profits they will be divided equally [i.e. by share]' after deduction of production costs (1655 Mentou gou); the 1873 Shanxi firm issued seventeen shares at 2,000 taels with profits distributed according to shares.

Not established. Zelin notes only that 'well-established practices governing liability for debt' inhibited acceptance of Western incorporation, without specifying what they were. This is the cell that would decide whether the Chinese partnership had owner shielding, and the article does not reach it.
Follows LR1. Not addressed.

Zelin's conclusion is that Chinese merchants' 'businesses could outlive them intact or survive the withdrawal of a partner'. Coded medium rather than high because that is a summary judgement in a conclusion rather than an attested clause; the supporting datum is the Tongren tang, founded 1669, surviving a fire in 1753 and a near-total dilution of its founding family, and still trading in the 1880s.
No terminal date in any contract cited; firms are recapitalised rather than wound up.

One party supplies capital and another labour, and the tradition says so in as many words: 'Those who put up capital are called silver shares (yingu). Those who put up labor are called body shares (shengu)' (Qingbai leichao). See hegu_shengu for the labour side.
Multiple principals as a matter of course — 45 shares across four parties at Mentou gou, seventeen shares in the 1873 Shanxi firm, twenty-four at the Mutaishangtang, thirty by custom at Ziliujing.

The claim arises from a 合约 heyue, a written partnership contract executed before a middleman and preserved in duplicate as evidence. The Ming model contract is explicit that the firm's money is not the partners' — 'He may not spend the firm's money and cause confusion in the accounts.'
Inapplicable: MG3 is meaningful only where MG1 is 'membership'. Propagated .NA.

NO STATE AUTHORISATION AT ALL, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF THE ARTICLE. Chinese imperial law 'left the regulation of most economic transactions to the normative realm and private contractual ordering'; the state gave force to private documents only by accepting them as evidence in dispute resolution. The 1904 company law is a transplant onto a tradition that had already done this work without it — only 227 companies were registered by 1908.
Trade, mining, milling, salt, banking, timber. No charitable or ritual purpose in the business partnerships.
Observed absence, and the contrast with kabu_local is the reason to record it. Nothing in the Chinese partnership confers an exclusive right; the share is a claim on income, not a licence to operate.

Observed absence rather than silence: Zelin's whole argument is that this tradition developed 'in the space vacated by state regulation', memorialised in private contracts, guild rules and ledgers rather than in any register. Land deeds were stamped and sealed by the state; business partnerships were not.

THE POINT OF CODING THIS CLASS SEPARATELY. Body-share holders 'had no claim to the equity of the firm, nor could their shares be inherited' (Morck and Yang on the Rishengchang bank). CI3=0 therefore sits inside the same firm as CI3=1 on hegu_yingu — a deliberately non-alienable claim alongside a freely alienable one, which is the decomposability argument in miniature.
Follows CI3. The claim is inseparable from the person who earned it; it exists because of who he is and what he does.

Proportional to shares held: clerks who did well 'were designated as shengu and they ceased to be paid wages. After 3 years, when the accounts were settled, the shengu received a portion of the profits commensurate with their shares.' A profit share replacing a wage.
The labour side of the asymmetry the tradition itself names: 身股 body shares against 銀股 silver shares, labour against capital.
Whether the body-share holder bore any part of a loss is not stated. He has no equity to lose, but whether a loss year simply produced no distribution or created an obligation is not addressed.
The claim arises from employment and designation, recorded in partnership contracts and ledgers.
Inapplicable: MG1 is not 'membership'. Propagated .NA.
An incentive instrument inside a profit-seeking firm; Zelin reads it as a solution to principal-agent problems across the Shanxi banks' branch networks.

UNIT MISMATCH, RECORDED RATHER THAN FORCED. TS1 asks whether the ENTITY persists across the death or exit of members; this row codes a share CLASS. The firm persists (see hegu_yingu TS1) while the body share extinguishes at death, converting into a term-limited 孤股 death share for the holder's kin. Entity-level characteristics are coded on hegu_yingu, which is the partnership itself; they are left .NR here rather than answered about the wrong object.

HALF-PRESENT AS A STRUCTURAL FACT, NOT AS A HEDGE. Kabu could be 'sold, borrowed, traded, inherited, increased, and generally treated like shares of stock' — but 'the movement of shares outside the geographical region defined by the society was prohibited', and 'Members could not sell or lease shares to brewers outside the defined region.' The distinction from hegu_yingu CI3=1 is principled rather than a matter of degree: a right of first refusal restricts WHO may buy within an open class of buyers, whereas the kabu's territorial rule restricts the CLASS ITSELF to licensed operators in one market. Alienable within a bounded population is P.

The certificate exists — brewing stock was evidenced by a wooden tag recording the holder's share — but the claim is not independent of the holder's identity, because holding it presupposes being a licensed brewer in the defined region. Negotiability is bounded by qualification.

THE CENSUS'S FIRST UNAMBIGUOUS FP2=1. The kabu IS the exclusive right, held as property: one share is a licence to operate one shop, manufactory, mill or scale, unlicensed brewing was suppressed by confiscating equipment, and 'Society members therefore had a monopoly on brewing for their particular market'. Contrast ortoq_loan FP2=.NR, where a state-run exclusionary trade regime was NOT a franchise the merchant owned.

The form is the status: ownership of stock functions as the licence to trade in that occupation, so the wrapper and the asset are the same object. Cleaner than the ortoq case, where the paiza was a privilege attached to the merchant rather than the instrument.

Stock societies were established or authorised by the state, membership was stock ownership, the number of shares fixed the number of members, and formation of unregulated commercial stock societies was banned. Legibility is constitutive here, not incidental.
'membership in kabu nakama depended on ownership of kabu'. The claim is membership in a body, and the share is the qualification for it.
Numerically restricted by construction: 'The number of shares available to a society determined the number of its members.' Applicable because MG1 is 'membership'.

Self-policing by collective rule: society regulations typically bound members not to deal with a member who cheated, not to hire an employee dismissed by another for misconduct, and to admit a former employee only on his old employer's introduction.

The state 'would establish something called stock, and ownership of shares in it acted as a license to operate a business in that occupation'. Brewing stock was created in 1660; in 1721 merchants, artisans and manufacturers were required to form and join stock societies under the Kyoho reforms. The opposite pole from hegu_yingu MG4=private-contract.
Societies persist across the turnover of members; shares are inherited and traded while the society continues. Medium — Nagata does not treat succession as such.
No terminal horizon; societies are standing bodies.
Brewing, wholesaling, silk brokerage, cotton textiles. Price control was a state purpose served BY the societies, not their members' declared purpose.
Observed absence. Membership is by licence held, not by a division of capital against labour; there is no capital-labour asymmetry internal to the share.
A society of many shareholding members.

THE CONTRAST CELL, AND THE REASON THIS ROW EXISTS. Sake shipped to the Edo market carried a separate class of brewing stock, priced separately from local-market shares, and 'Unlike the local shares, Edo export shares could be sold or traded outside the region or market of the original license.' One tradition, two classes, opposite values on the transferable-claims component.
Alienable beyond the licensing region, but still a brewing licence and so still tied to qualification. P rather than 1: Nagata does not say the buyer could be a non-brewer.
Still a franchise held as property — the export share carried access to more rice and the right to greater production volume.
Part of the same state-established brewing stock as kabu_local.
Held by members of certain societies; the share qualifies the holder.
Sake brewing for the Edo market.
Held within societies of many members. Coded thinly on purpose — this row's value is the CI3 contrast with kabu_local and not independent structural evidence.

Shares in corporate deity associations were bought, inherited and sold, and 'These shares were treated in the same way that sales of land were treated' — some designated irrevocable sales, others redeemable by the original owner at a later date. The surviving contracts are mostly records of such sales.

Half-present: the share is an abstract income claim traded like land, but the redeemable form (典 dian conditional sale) keeps the original owner's identity live in the instrument. Negotiable in the irrevocable form, not in the conditional one.
A corporate estate: the association holds land, and several contracts state the acreage, location and expected rents.

'if there was a surplus after the ritual functions of the association were performed, the remaining income from rents would be distributed among the shareholders.' Proportional to shares, not a fixed claim.

The association outlives its donors — the surviving contracts are sales by entities that 'had either inherited them or purchased them from other shareholders', generations after the founding donations.
A standing estate supporting recurring annual ritual; no horizon.
Shareholding IS membership of the association, acquired originally by donation of land or assets 'commensurate with their largesse'.

Felloni glosses the institution's own Latin name: Casa, 'or more precisely Officium in Latin, denotes a body with its own legal identity (in that it survives the succession of those managing it), performing a specific function via the management of a group of assets. These are administered in an autonomous manner, within the limits set by the law.' He says the same of each compera: it 'had its own legal identity, survived over time even if the lenders ceded their quota to a third party'. ANACHRONISM WARNING, RAISED BY THE SOURCE ITSELF AND NOT BY THE CODER. Taviani 2022, 15 identifies the modern definitional bundle - 'locked-in capital', 'tradable shares', 'legal personhood', 'separation of ownership and management', 'limited liability' - and argues that its application to San Giorgio is the Historische Rechtsschule's anachronism: a concept 'derived from later companies (VOC and EIC) and superimposed on an earlier institution'. That bundle is very nearly this dataset's declared WP2 set. See the adjudications note; this cell is coded on Felloni's statement of legal identity, not on the bundle.

Felloni: 'The Casa di San Giorgio ran the bank in its own name and at its own risk.' Taviani 115: San Giorgio acquired territories by translatio and held them with plena iurisdictio; the transferring contracts from Famagusta (1447) name San Giorgio as the party taking. Coded high because ownership in the entity's name is attested for two different classes of asset (the banks and the territories) by two independent authors. Articulation left .NR: neither author quotes a constitutive clause verbatim, and the 1447 contracts would settle it if read.

One attested instance: in 1456, when San Giorgio created a secondary market of pagae, a lawsuit concerning Caffa was brought to the papal court of Callixtus III. Taviani reports it as an action of Battista Fregoso, a protettore acting in San Giorgio's interest, rather than plainly as the entity suing in its own name, so this is P and not 1. THE EVIDENCE BASE HERE IS THIN AND THE TERM COUNT SAYS SO: 'personalit*' occurs twice in Taviani's 264 pages and once in Petti Balbi. Legal personality is not what this literature is about, and LP1-LP3 should not be read as though it were.

The books of contracts of San Giorgio, which Taviani 57 uses for the confiscation immunity, are where an answer would be found.

notes: A holder cannot demand his capital back from the compera. Repayment of the principal was the state's option, at its discretion, and was often converted de facto into perpetual debt. Taviani 57 adds the harder case from the books of contracts: neither loca nor pagae could be confiscated, 'not by the Commune, not by San Giorgio', not even for lese-majeste. NOTE THE DIRECTION. That last clause protects the MEMBER's asset from the entity and the state; AP2 asks whether members and their creditors can force partition of the ENTITY's assets. The two are not the same fact and the cell rests on the first source, not the second.

No source in this batch establishes whether a holder of loca could be pursued by the venture's own creditors beyond his subscription. An unevidenced 'limited' here would have been the single most consequential error available in this coding.

No founder. San Giorgio was constituted in 1407 by the existing creditors of the Commune out of the consolidation of the compere, not endowed out of any person's patrimony. AP4 is written around a founder and a corpus and is flagged in CHARACTER-CODING.md as waqf-shaped; the same .NA that bazacle_mill takes.

Felloni's gloss of Officium turns on precisely this - a body that 'survives the succession of those managing it' - and he says of the compera that it 'survived over time even if the lenders ceded their quota to a third party'. The institution ran 1407-1805. Articulation .NR: the Latin term is contemporary but the gloss is Felloni's.

The Casa is open-ended, 1407-1805. Do not confuse this with the individual compera, which Felloni sec. 2 describes as a medium-to-long-term loan, 'generally 5 years or longer', with its own name and term. The type row names the Casa, so the horizon is the Casa's; the fixed-term character of the constituent compere is recorded here rather than in the cell.

Whether any party could dissolve or unwind San Giorgio at will is not established by the material read. The question is live rather than absent: the Commune's attempts to redeem the compere and reabsorb the institution are the subject of Taviani's chapters 7-8, which this coding did not read in full (source_read=partial throughout). In the maona contracts the parallel right is explicit - the Commune may redeem the loca at a fixed 75 lire each (Taviani 30) - so the analogous San Giorgio provision, if it exists, is findable. Left .NR rather than 0 for that reason.

San Giorgio altered its own constitution repeatedly by internal decision: election regulations in 1411, council regulations in 1425, the banking rule of 1437, the regulae of 1463, further changes in 1518, and new statutes at the reform of 1568. Taviani 56 is explicit that the 1411 change 'moved the process from the Commune to the Compere of San Giorgio, because at that point the investors chose the protettori'. P rather than 1 because the authority is shared and Taviani describes the 1463 regulae as 'the statutes of Genoa', so rule-making over San Giorgio was never wholly internal. P here is structural half-presence, not hedging; the uncertainty that does exist is carried by confidence.

Felloni: 'The sum on loan to the state was the compera's capital and, to facilitate the collection of the money which was to be loaned, it was subdivided into shares with a nominal value of 100 units of account, without materiality and known as luoghi.' One capital, subdivided; not several accounts.

Contributed capital is not withdrawable at will: the subscription becomes the compera's capital, the return arrives as an assigned tax revenue, and liquidity is obtained by selling the luogo rather than by redemption. Overlaps AP2 by the vocabulary's own admission (AP2's definition flags the pair as a candidate for merger rather than grouping); the two are coded here on the same passages and SHOULD NOT BE COUNTED AS TWO WITNESSES to lock-in.

Luoghi 'were registered against the individual lenders, could be transferred to a third party by simple registration in the official creditors' ledgers' and 'were actively traded, also for speculation' (Felloni sec. 2). Taviani 57: 'anyone, not only Genoese citizens, could invest in San Giorgio's shares'; at 30 the maona contracts state the rule in the tradition's own voice - participants 'can sell their shares to anyone they want'. Articulated because transfer by registration is a procedure the institution operated and recorded, not a modern description of it.

THE DISCRIMINATING CELL, AND THE ONE THE LITERATURE WARNS ABOUT. Toward 1: the luogo is immaterial ('without materiality'), of standard nominal value, transferable by registration, actively traded and used for speculation. Against 1: it is 'registered against the individual lenders', transferable only by formal entry in a nominal ledger, and 'sometimes accompanied by legal privilege'. Miner 2020, 82 is the substantive objection - 'family, patrimony, and lineage were at least as central to Genoese thinking about public debt as profit and markets', with women outnumbering men as participants by 1367 and a corresponding shift in the profile of holders. An interest routinely settled in dowry and inheritance is not yet negotiable independently of who holds it. P, on the bazacle_mill and asiento_averia precedent, and the market and the patrimony are both real.

Same position as AP3, and for the same reason. Nothing read establishes the extent or form of a holder's liability to San Giorgio's third-party creditors. Where a source addresses only the relation between holder and institution, this cell is .NR rather than a value carried over.

The decision-makers are required by statute to be substantial holders: the 24 probi cives were chosen from those who had invested at least 1,000 lire in loca, the eight protettori were elected from the same group, and after 1463 the electors had to hold at least 30 loca (merchants) or 15 (artisans), raised again in 1518 and set at 25 in 1568. A governing body defined by a shareholding qualification is exposed to the entity's outcomes by construction.

Return is a proportional share of an assigned tax revenue, not a fixed claim, and Felloni gives the tradition's own reason for it: the yield 'could vary from year to year depending on economic trends, sometimes exceeding but, more often than not, falling short of the sum initially expected. This brought an element of uncertainty to the capital/interest ratio for the creditors, thereby avoiding the automatism of a fixed interest which the Church, in those times, would have condemned as unlawful earnings.' Articulated: the canon-law rationale is stated, not reconstructed. TERMINOLOGY, PER CLAUDE.md. What varies here is an UNCERTAINTY, not a priced distribution - no one sold the variance to a party without a stake. Felloni's own gloss, 'similar to today's index-linked bonds', names the endpoint of a shift as though it had always obtained and is not inherited here.

No mutualisation of idiosyncratic member risk. Every holder of a given compera is exposed to one and the same thing, the yield of the assigned tax; nothing member-specific is pooled and no member is indemnified by the others. Coded 0 rather than .NR because Felloni describes the mechanism completely enough to support an observed absence, on the bazacle_mill LR4=0 precedent. LR5 is .NA in consequence, and the .NA is consistent with the 0 rather than diagnostic against it - contrast waqf_khayri, where an .NA on LR5 was what exposed LR4=P as an error.
LR4 is 0, so there are no pooled baskets whose correlation could be asked about. Propagated .NA per the vocabulary's applicability_on.

LR2 is not 'veiled', so the cell exists, but nothing read states the DIRECTION of the protettori's exposure. The shareholding qualification (LR2) establishes that they were exposed; it does not establish that they shared gains and losses alike rather than asymmetrically, and inferring 'symmetric' from the same passage would manufacture a second observation out of one. Left .NR deliberately. Note for the maintainer: LR6 exists precisely because LR2 was found to bundle two questions, and answering the second from the first would undo that repair.

Coded on the bazacle_mill and asiento_averia precedent. Taviani's sources call the participants 'owners of the Compere' and treat them as a body that elects its own officers from among its number. TENSION RECORDED RATHER THAN RESOLVED: the claim originates in a purchase - a subscription to a loan, evidenced by a tradable security - which points to 'contract', while the governance rights and the electoral body point to 'membership'. The two readings are not distinguished by the value set, and this row takes the reading its two nearest coded analogues take.

Elected office throughout, under successively restated statutes: 1411 election regulations dividing offices between nobles and populares; the 24 probi cives and the eight outgoing protettori electing the eight new ones; a mixed procedure of election and lot described in the sources as 'ad voces et ad balotolas'; 40 shareholders needed for a valid council after 1425; 32 electors under the 1568 statutes. Protettori held office for one year and could not immediately take other San Giorgio posts, the bar extending to relatives to the third degree of cognation and the second of agnation. Articulated: these are the institution's own regulae. Taviani 56 records that Heers thought San Giorgio unrepresentative because offices were 'chosen and not elected'; Taviani disagrees, and the disagreement is about degree, not about whether the locus was collective.

'Since anyone, not only Genoese citizens, could invest in San Giorgio's shares' (Taviani 57), and foreigners - people from Asti among them - did. Holding is not closed and not numerically capped. A POSSIBLE CONFLATION, FLAGGED AND NOT REPAIRED, PER CLAUDE.md. What IS restricted is the franchise, not the membership: only male holders above a threshold of loca could vote or hold office (Taviani 56, 'only male owners of a certain number of loca could vote'), with the threshold restated in 1463, 1518 and 1568. MG3's locator is members and its definition asks whether membership is closed; it has no way to record a body whose membership is open and whose franchise is property- and sex-qualified. Recorded here because this is where the evidence lives; a repair, if one is warranted, belongs in a later commit and not in the batch that motivated it.

Constituted in 1407 out of the Commune's consolidation of its compere, and its later powers came by grant from the Commune - Taviani 115 describes the territorial acquisitions as translatio, with the contracts from Famagusta (1447) onward conveying merum et mixtum imperium, ius gladii and plena iurisdictio. NOTE, AND IT MATTERS FOR THE MAONA ROW TOO: Taviani observes that these contracts 'contain terms that were used in feudal transfers of the previous centuries'. The authorising instrument is in feudal form; what it conveys is not feudal. state-charter records the source of authority, not the idiom of the document.

Exclusive rights held as property, in two layers. The compera itself IS a purchased right to collect a named tax for the term of the loan - Felloni sec. 2: assuming the role of creditor 'meant buying a specific tax revenue in exchange for a certain price'. Above that, from the Famagusta contracts of 1447 onward San Giorgio held merum et mixtum imperium, ius gladii and plena iurisdictio over its territories (Taviani 115). Distinguish from a trading monopoly, which San Giorgio did not have: Felloni sec. 9 contrasts it with the Bank of England, which 'obtained a monopoly over all banking activities'.

Holding loca conferred a legal immunity obtainable no other way. From the books of contracts of San Giorgio, 'neither loca nor pagae could be confiscated - not by the Commune, not by San Giorgio - not even for the crime of lese-majeste', and this ran to heads of factions such as the Adorno and Fregoso and to any person involved in political crimes. Combined with the openness recorded at MG3 - anyone, including non-citizens, could hold - that is legal-status arbitrage in the plain sense of FP3's definition. Taviani immediately qualifies it: 'in the long run both Genoese and Florentine political offices stopped respecting these agreements and laws', and the Commune did try to seize an external investor's loca. Coded 1 for the period the contracts govern, with the erosion recorded here rather than as a lower value. Articulation .NR because Taviani reports the clause without quoting it.

Official creditors' ledgers recording every holder and every transfer; accounts 'kept by a notary of the College, filed by year and kept in a double-entry accounting system'; the libri delle pagae recording annual interest. The institution is legible to the Commune by construction, since the Commune is its counterparty.

No capital-labour asymmetry. The protettori are not agents supplying enterprise against someone else's capital; they are elected from among the investors and are required to be substantial holders themselves. Salaried staff existed - governors of the banks were chosen 'from amongst the best of the staff in the office' (Felloni sec. 6) - but employment is not the asymmetry CF1 names.
CF1 is 0, so there is no working party who could bear loss of a principal's capital. Propagated .NA per applicability_on.
Many principals throughout: the compera is subscribed by a body of lenders, a valid council after 1425 required 40 shareholders, and the 1437 banking rule required a council of 300 citizen-investors.

Whether the maona was a legal person distinct from the maonesi is never asked.

Pulls both ways and the cell records the tension rather than resolving it. FOR: the maona acted and was acted against as such - a petition is made 'ad requisitionem participum mahone Corsice', and the article names an 'olim stipendiarius della maona di Corsica', so it engaged and paid servants. AGAINST: the 1378 cession conveyed the island to the feudatari personally, and money spent on the island is 'i quattrini' owed back pro quota to individual partecipi, not to a fund - Napoleone Lomellini sues for 'la parte spettante al figlio'. Property looks joint rather than entity-held.

No litigation by or against the maona as an entity is discussed; the suits reported at 161-162 run between individual maonesi and their debtors.

Whether the maona's creditors ranked before a maonese's personal creditors in the common assets is not addressed. The debt episodes at 161-162 are individual obligations between participants, which is evidence about persons and not about a partitioned estate.

Whether a participant or his creditors could force partition is not addressed. The one structural fact adjacent to it - that the ten quote persist and change hands - is coded at CI3 and TS1 and must not be re-read here as a second observation.

The ten-quota structure persists across the death and exit of individuals: quote are transferred and inherited - Andreolo Figone's quota passes and its acquirer 'potrebbe essere entrato nella maona' - and in 1407, at the very end, 'si ricordano ancora dieci soci'. Twenty-nine years, changing membership, constant structure. The maona's termination in 1407 is TS2's question, not this one.

Formally an enfeoffment: the 1378 cession is 'in feudum rectum, nobile et gentile', with the six attributes of vassalic fidelity, a horse worth 40 gold florins each Pentecost 'in signum subiectionis', and the doge touching the kneeling feudatories with the baculus. 'Un gruppo eterogeneo di persone accomunate dal solo desiderio del guadagno', and to Corsican eyes 'un vero e proprio strumento di colonizzazione e di sfruttamento'. DECISION BY MS, 2026-08-29: coded 1 rather than P. FILLS A VALUE THAT HAD NO INSTANCE ANYWHERE IN THIS DATASET. The Commune held a unilateral, optional power to unwind the arrangement by buying it out: it 'can redeem with a fixed term the territories, acquiring all the loca from the participants in the Old Maona; if the redemption fails, the Commune can later try again to acquire the loca at the fixed price of 75 lire for each locum', with named windows - by 22 February 1366, then a four-year wait, then four years to try again. THE REASONING FOR 1 OVER P: the windows constrain WHEN the power may be exercised, not WHETHER; nothing conditions the redemption on the participants' conduct, consent or default; and the price is fixed in advance, so the holders cannot resist by pricing. That is a revocable arrangement in TS3's sense - dissolvable at one party's option - and the periodicity is a term of the option, not a limit on it. THE READING FOR P, RECORDED BECAUSE IT WAS REAL: a power exercisable only in three defined windows across eight years is not continuously available, and 'at will' in the characteristic's definition can be read to require continuous availability. Whoever revisits this should know the cell was contested and decided, not obvious. NOTE ALSO WHAT THE VALUE DOES NOT SAY: revocability here belongs to the GRANTOR, not to a member or a founder. TS3's locator is the arrangement and the value set does not record which party holds the power, so this cell reads the same as a founder-revocable waqf would. That is a limitation worth carrying into any comparison that uses it.

A grant from the Commune, which retains the fullest juridical power over the island through its podestà and 'can revise the account books of the territorial administration'. Buyers of shares are subject to the doge's will. The authority is the Commune's throughout.

The mastic monopoly, confirmed to the Old Maona in the 1362 settlement - 'they continue to have a monopoly on mastic' - together with ownership and administration of the island. AN INTERNAL DISCREPANCY IN THE SOURCE, RECORDED RATHER THAN RESOLVED, AND IT IS ABOUT SOVEREIGNTY RATHER THAN MONOPOLY. At 27 Taviani contrasts the Elba maona with Chios and Corsica, implying Chios held sovereign rights. Against that: at 26 the 1346 contract gives the investors plena iurisdictio and ius gladii ONLY CONTINGENTLY, 'in the event of the fall of the regime of Genoa'; Table 1.1 for 1347 assigns merum et mixtum imperium to the Commune through its podestà, the participants obtaining full territorial power only 'in the case of a collapse of the Commune of Genoa'; and at 85 n. Taviani states flatly, citing Tinterri, that the Giustiniani 'had administered a maona in Chios WITHOUT the plena iurisdictio'. Three statements against one passing contrast: THE MAONA OF CHIOS HELD A MONOPOLY AND AN ADMINISTRATION BUT NOT SOVEREIGN JURISDICTION. Contrast maona_corsica, where Taviani 27 says the Commune granted the island 'with sovereign powers such as the merum et mixtum imperium' and the investors 'were considered the equivalent of feudal lords' - which is compatible with Petti Balbi's finding that the feudal form masked an appalto, since the form was real even where the substance was commercial.

The form gave private investors the ownership and administration of a territory and its monopoly, which they could not have held individually, and entry was reserved to populares - a status qualification that made membership itself a political position. P and not 1 because the sovereign status stayed with the Commune's podestà; what the maonesi got was administration, not jurisdiction.

Legible to the granting authority by construction: the Commune 'can revise the account books of the territorial administration', the loca carry a fixed redemption price, and the participants' numbers and status are prescribed. Grotius makes mederederschap a species of societas combined with a communio of joint owners (De ruysscher 2023, 337, on Inleidinge iii.23.1, iii.20.46, iii.28-29); whether the rederij is a person distinct from the reders is never asked. The nearest passage is Lehmann's claim that the ship 'was considered a corpus', so that creditors of ship debts had the ship as preferential object of enforcement (353). That is reported as Lehmann's 1895 thesis and De ruysscher's own comment on the next page is that Lehmann was retrojecting the German Aktiengesellschaft of 1870/1884 (354). Not admissible as evidence for this cell.

Ownership is fractional co-ownership by the reders (357-358), not property held by an association - but whether a rederij could take or hold property in its own name is not a question the article asks, and the fractional-ownership statement answers CI1, not this. Coding 0 here would launder a silence into an asserted absence.

No litigation by or against a rederij as an entity is discussed. Every action De ruysscher analyses - actio exercitoria, actio institoria, actio pro socio - runs against the reders individually or against the shipmaster (344-346).

Whether creditors of the ship or the expedition ranked before a reder's personal creditors in the common assets is not addressed. Lehmann's corpus claim at 353 asserts that entity creditors had the ship as preferential object of enforcement, which is a different proposition, and is reported rather than endorsed - see LP1.

Whether a reder or his personal creditors could force partition or withdrawal is never asked. The adjacent fact - the right of abandonment - is a liability escape triggered by a specific claim, not a partition right, and is coded at AP3 and LR1; it must not be re-read here as a second observation. De ruysscher expressly leaves the consequences of one reder's abandonment for the remaining reders unresolved (363).

LOCATOR: CF1 is P, so the cell takes the labour-party - the shipmaster participating as partner without a share in the ship. HERE THE LOCATOR DOES NOT CHANGE THE VALUE, which is worth recording explicitly: the source states the same rule for the reders as members. Grotius caps the reder at his 'aendeel' in the ship plus what he 'further has in the reedinge' (Inleidinge iii.1.32, iii.20.48; ibp ii.11.13 'eorum quae in navi sunt'), and the participating shipmaster 'forfeits the remuneration for his labour' and nothing beyond it (341). De ruysscher reads the cap as reaching third parties, while noting that 'Grotius does not enter into this point' (342). P RATHER THAN 1 FOR TWO STRUCTURAL REASONS, NOT FOR UNCERTAINTY: (i) the Antwerp Consuetudines Compilatae of 1608 deny abandonment where the reders themselves hired the crew that caused the damage, on culpa in eligendo (348); (ii) the shield is dispositive and was contracted around - vault note [[The Bodmerei shield was a default rule and Amsterdam contracted out of it]], where Amsterdam bodemerij protests of 1601-21 execute against 'die personen van den voorn. schipper ende sijn reders ende alle haere andere goederen'. CONFIDENCE LOW ON THE SOURCE'S OWN DATING ARGUMENT: De ruysscher holds that a general right of abandonment 'did not exist before Grotius put it to text' (350-351) and that Grotius 'stood on the sideline' of the development (363). This cell records a jurist's rule of c.1619-1625, not an attested practice of the fifteenth-century partenrederij.

No founder and no corpus constituted out of a founder's patrimony: the arrangement is entered by purchase of parts. Same disposition as bazacle_mill, casa_san_giorgio, maona_chios and maona_corsica. AP4 is written around a waqf-shaped founder and is flagged as such in the vocabulary.

This is precisely the question De ruysscher declares unresolved: 'How according to Grotius reders had to cope with a peer who abandoned his share when being confronted with a debt that was too high is unclear. One can surmise that in that case the debt accrued to the other reders if they agreed to perpetuate their venture of co-ownership' (363). A surmise about continuation, offered as a surmise, is not a coding.

WHAT THE SOURCE SUPPORTS IS A NEGATIVE. The co-ownership outlasts any one expedition: co-owners 'can refrain from participating in a particular expedition with the ship in which they have fractional ownership' (341, on Inleidinge iii.23.3), and De ruysscher separates 'deel hebben' (having a share in ownership) from 'reeden' (participating as partner in an expedition) on the same page. That rules out single-venture, and so separates the partenrederij from commenda, societas_maris and qirad, which all carry TS2=single-venture. WHAT IT DOES NOT SUPPORT is the positive content of 'open': no term is stated, and the natural horizon is the life of the ship rather than an indefinite one. Low and analyst-imposed accordingly. .NR IS THE DEFENSIBLE ALTERNATIVE and is put to the maintainer.

Grotius's rule on resignation (Inleidinge iii.21.8: a withdrawing partner may not do so in a way that harms the partnership) is expressly disapplied to mederederschap at iii.21.9, and De ruysscher calls the substitution 'hardly convincing' without saying what the substituted rule is (364). The source records that the question has an answer and does not supply it.
Whether the reders could alter the arrangement's rules or purpose by internal decision is not addressed.

'Such partenrederij had been used at least since the beginning of the fifteenth century. It was a fractional joint ownership, which allowed for pooling investments in costly ships' (357-358). Undivided fractional shares in one vessel, held in communio: common, not several accounts. FLAGGED: De ruysscher distinguishes this from the open rederij, where 'the participants... were simple investors in a stock that was not the ship itself' (358), and observes that the two ran together in practice, Grotius included. If the maintainer folds the open rederij into this type row, CI1 spans both values and the standing rule requires a split. THIS ROW CODES THE PARTENREDERIJ STRICTLY.

Whether a reder could withdraw contributed capital at will is not addressed. The right of abandonment is not a withdrawal right: it is triggered by a claim and cedes the part in satisfaction of it. Whether he could sell out is CI3's question and is likewise unrecorded.

THE CELL I MOST EXPECTED TO FILL AND CANNOT. De ruysscher never says whether a ship part was alienable, and the two adjacent statements are about other things: van Brakel's 'shares in the former could in principle not be passed on to others' (353) concerns general partnerships, not rederijen, and the vibrant secondary market at 364 is in VOC shares. Scammell 1962, 114 has English ship shares divided, consolidated and transferred with 'amazing speed and facility', but that is the English form; importing it is the move the vocabulary's MG4 note exists to forbid. See the adjudications.
CI4 entails CI3, which is .NR. Nothing in the source bears on whether a part was negotiable independently of its holder's identity.

LOCATOR as at AP3, and again the value does not turn on it. Grotius gives three variants for trading partners - in solidum; proportionate and unlimited (pro parte, the Holland rule); and 'the third variant, limited liability, according to Grotius applies for reders only. This liability is proportionate as well, but limited to what they invest and gain in the expedition for which the debt is incurred' (343). In ibp ii.11.13 the cap is 'the value of the ship and of the merchandise in the ship' (336). THE DISSENT IS COMPRESSED HERE AND THE MAINTAINER SHOULD SEE IT: where the shield was contracted around - the Amsterdam bodemerij acts of the vault note - the reders were proportionate and UNLIMITED, i.e. unlimited-several. LR1's allowed_values contain no 'mixed' cell of the kind that holds the Harris v. Le Bris/Goetzmann/Pouget dispute open at bazacle_mill FP1, so a nominal choice here compresses a real disagreement. RECORDED, NOT REPAIRED: no new value is proposed. Same dating caveat as AP3.

The reders are principals; the shipmaster is their agent acting 'int stuck van sijn ampt'. The reders take the expedition's profits and bear its losses in proportion to stake, capped at that stake - 'participants venture with what they have at stake in the expedition, and nothing more' (340). A cap bounds exposure; it does not veil it. Every other capped form in this matrix - voc_1602, voc_1612, voc_1623, asiento_averia - also reads coupled.

Proportionality to stake is what Grotius states for Holland against the Roman in solidum rule: partners 'each pay a share of the debt corresponding to their stake in the business (pro parte)' (335), and for reders the liability 'is proportionate as well' (343). Returns follow the same fractions of the ship. NOT CODED FROM LEHMANN, whose claim that shares partitioned 'both in the ships and profits' (353-354) De ruysscher reports and then criticises as retrojection.

THE FORM DIVIDES ONE EXPOSURE; IT DOES NOT MUTUALISE MEMBER-SPECIFIC ONES. Fractional joint ownership 'allowed for pooling investments in costly ships' (357-358): the pooling is of capital into a single bottom, so every reder's exposure is the same hazard and nothing idiosyncratic to a member is pooled or indemnified. Identical structure and identical value to maona_corsica LR4=0, where 'the maonesi share one common exposure, the island'. TWO THINGS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED, BOTH FLAGGED FOR ADJUDICATION: (i) general average and the gemeenschap des uitkomsts (337-338, 349) do mutualise an idiosyncratic loss, but across the ship-and-cargo venture rather than across the membership of the rederij, and general average is coded in loss_mitigation_forms; (ii) a merchant holding sixteenths in many bottoms diversifies, but that is a fact about his portfolio rather than about this form, and the evidence for it is English (Scammell 1962, 115), not from this source. 0 RATHER THAN .NR IS A JUDGEMENT: De ruysscher describes the structure well enough to answer the question but never poses it in these terms. The conservative alternative is .NR.

LR4 is 0, so there are no pooled baskets whose correlation could be asked about. LR2 is not veiled, so the cell exists. The reders share the expedition's gains and bear its losses to the extent of their stake - proportionate in both directions (343). The shipmaster who participates as partner is on the same footing: he ventures 'for a share of the profits' instead of a fixed wage (341, on Inleidinge iii.20.46 and iii.23.2) and on a bad outcome 'forfeits the remuneration for his labour' (341). Neither party holds a call option bounded below at zero. SEPARATES the partenrederij from commenda, qirad and ortoq_equity (LR6=upside-only); agrees with societas_maris.

Genuinely ambiguous in the source and not resolved by it. The reder's claim rests on his fractional ownership, which reads as membership; but Grotius makes mederederschap a species of societas, a contract (337, Inleidinge iii.23.1), and De ruysscher's argument is that communio and societas were blended rather than separated (346-347). Forcing a choice would manufacture a value the source does not have.

The reders are principals in the plural who mandate a shipmaster-agent: De ruysscher writes throughout of 'the reders' as the body that gives funds to, and is bound by the acts of, its agent (340), and treats the voorcompagnie directors as 'agents of the investors' on the same analogy (364). The locus of decision is therefore the body of co-owners, not a founder and not a single principal. LOW, AND ONE THING DECLINED: Lehmann's 'each co-owner of the ship had a say according to the share in the ship and expedition' (353) would give per-share voting, but De ruysscher immediately reads that as Lehmann importing the shareholders' meeting of the German Aktienrecht of 1870/1884 (354). The voting rule is not coded.

MG1 is .NR, so applicability cannot be settled: .NA here would assert that MG1 is contract or beneficiary, which is not established, and check_dependence.py would rightly flag it as SUSPECT. Nothing in the source bears on whether membership was closed or numerically restricted in any case.

A COMPARATIVE-CONCEPT PROBLEM, NOT ONLY A GAP. The partenrederij required no authorisation: it is constituted by the purchase of parts, and its rules come from maritime custom and local law - the Amsterdam Ordinancie, the princely statutes of 1551 and 1563, the Antwerp customs, the Hanseatic sealaw (348-350). 'customary' would describe the source of its RULES and 'private-contract' the source of its CONSTITUTION; MG4 asks for one answer because it was built for entities that need authorising. Left .NR and the misfit flagged alongside the vocabulary's existing notes on AP4, MG4 and FP4.

Grotius defines maatschap, of which mederederschap is a species, as 'a venture with the aim of making profits out of communal goods or service' (337, on Inleidinge iii.21.1), and the ships are held for 'maritime trading expeditions' (358). No pious, charitable or mutual-provision purpose appears anywhere in the article.

Whether a rederij held any exclusive right or franchise is not addressed. The chartered monopoly in this article belongs to the VOC (351, 361), a different form, already coded as voc_1602/voc_1612/voc_1623.
Whether the form conferred legal-status or access arbitrage on its principals is not addressed.

Not addressed. The nearest regulatory material - the 1611 ordinance of the Estates of Holland making reders answerable for damage caused by their fishermen up to the value of ship and cargo (350) - is a liability rule imposed on reders, not evidence that a rederij was registered or otherwise legible as an entity to political authority. FP4's 'political authority' is one of the three characteristics the vocabulary already flags as poorly exported.

HALF-PRESENT BECAUSE THE FORM RUNS BOTH WAYS AND THE SOURCE SAYS SO. 'Shipmasters who do not co-own the ship are allowed to participate in the venture of a voyage with the jointly owned ship and can then be considered partners in the project. Under those circumstances they do not receive a fixed wage, but instead venture for a share of the profits' (341, on Inleidinge iii.20.46 and iii.23.2) - there the labour party IS a party to the arrangement. But 'shipmasters are commonly co-owners' (341), in which case the members are alike and there is no asymmetry; and where the shipmaster takes a fixed wage he is an employee rather than a party. THE VALUE DRIVES THE AP3 AND LR1 LOCATOR, so this is not a cosmetic cell - see those notes, where the source happens to give the same rule under either locator. THE ALTERNATIVE IS 0, on the ground that the partenrederij strictly is a co-ownership among capital-supplying parties and the shipmaster is its agent, not its member. PUT TO THE MAINTAINER, together with the observation that the repo's standing rule - a type spanning both values of a characteristic must be split, as voc was on 2026-08-29 - would on one reading require a split here rather than a P.

CF1 is P, so the cell exists. The working party does not bear loss of the principals' capital: the participating shipmaster 'forfeits the remuneration for his labour' (341) and nothing further, while the ship and the stake in the reeding are the reders' to lose. Same configuration as commenda, qirad, ortoq_equity and voc_1602. THIS IS CF2'S QUESTION AND NOT AP3'S, per the repair of 2026-08-18: the shipmaster's exposure to third-party creditors of the venture is AP3; his exposure to the principals' capital is here.

Fractional joint ownership among co-owners in the plural, 'which allowed for pooling investments in costly ships' (357-358); Grotius defines mederederschap as 'two or more reders' co-owning a ship or engaged in a communal enterprise with it (337, Inleidinge iii.23.1). QUALIFICATION RECORDED: the article notes that a single reder is also possible and limitedly liable on the same rule (340, footnote 11, on Inleidinge iii.20.17), so the form admits a degenerate case; the type is nonetheless the multi-party one.

THE FIRST 1 ON THIS CHARACTERISTIC IN THE MATRIX, and it is not a thin one. The beguinages litigate as bodies, repeatedly, and on both sides of the record: the Diest butchers' guild sued the Beguines in the 1670s; the Leuven bakers' guild 'brought suit against the city's Grand Beguinage (and lost)' in 1681; the Mechelen Beguines ran a conflict with the local brewers' guild 'that went on for over half a century'; and 'it was the mistresses who fought these legal battles on their communities' behalves' (85-86). Grand mistresses also 'appealed to their cities and regional councils, and rather less frequently to their Habsburg governors and even the crown' (80), and Fernandina de Bock appealed to Carlos II successfully 'at least five times during her tenure' (86). Contrast waqf_khayri, asiento_averia, bazacle_mill and casa_san_giorgio, all P.

Whether the sub-institutions' creditors ranked before a beguine's personal creditors in institutional assets is not addressed. The nearby fact - that no sub-institution 'could be held responsible for the others' debts' (Moran 77) - is shielding BETWEEN SIBLING ENTITIES, not between the entity and its members, and it is coded at LP1 and CI1. Re-reading it here would count one datum twice.

Whether a beguine or her creditors could force partition or withdrawal of institutional assets is never asked. There is a structural reason to think the question could not arise - a beguine holds a lijfrent, a lifetime lease, rather than a share (Moran 77) - but that is coded at CI2 and CI3, and inferring 1 from the absence of shares would be laundering. Note that Moran does record the institution selling houses when numbers dipped (77), which is the entity partitioning its own assets, not a member forcing it.

CF1 is 0, so the locator reverts to members - the beguines. Whether an institutional creditor could reach a beguine's personal estate is not addressed by any source read. .NA WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: waqf_khayri carries .NA here because a waqf has no members whose liability could be asked about, but the begijnhof does have a membership (MG1=membership) that elects its own head, so the question exists and is simply unanswered. This is the main reason the WP1 owner-shielding component is empty for this form.

In exchange for these benefits, convent Beguines PRAYED FOR THE DONORS' SOULS' - and those bodies are 'likewise financially self-sufficient' (78), each with a convent mistress who 'maintained their houses' finances' (79).
